papers.title: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable,Navigable, and Editable

summary.tldr: The Harness Handbook is a behavior-centric representation, synthesized via static analysis and LLM-assisted structuring, that links agent harness behaviors to source code, improving localization and edit-plan quality for evolving AI agents.
key_points: Introduces the Harness Handbook, an automatically synthesized, behavior-centric representation of an agent harness codebase.
The Handbook uses static analysis and LLM-assisted structuring to link specific behaviors to their corresponding source code locations.
Introduces Behavior-Guided Progressive Disclosure (BGPD) to guide agents from high-level behaviors to implementation details and verify candidate locations.
Handbook-Assisted planning improves behavior localization and edit-plan quality, particularly for scattered sites, rarely executed paths, and cross-module interactions.
The method reduces planner token usage during modification requests on open-source harnesses.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach addresses the bottleneck of behavior localization in evolving AI agent harnesses, making modifications more efficient and accurate.

papers.title: Boogu-Image-0.1: Boosting Open Agentic Multimodal Generation via Understanding under a Minimal Budget

summary.tldr: Boogu-Image-0.1 is an open-source unified multimodal understanding and generation model family achieving competitive performance with a minimal budget through enhanced understanding capabilities and data quality improvements.
key_points: Boogu-Image-0.1 includes Base, Turbo, Edit, and Edit-Turbo variants for text-to-image generation, fast inference, instruction-based editing, and bilingual text rendering.
Performance is enhanced by a stronger multimodal encoder, agentic prompt rewriting, improved data quality, and optimized training pipelines.
The model was trained on 208.62 million unique images with a theoretical training cost of approximately $400K.
Boogu-Image-0.1 matches or surpasses other open-source models and approaches leading closed-source systems on standard benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: This work demonstrates that high-performance multimodal generation and editing can be achieved with significantly constrained compute budgets, making advanced AI more accessible.

papers.title: Ring-Zero: Scaling Zero RL to a Trillion Parameters for Emergent Reasoning

summary.tldr: Ring-Zero scales zero-RL to 1 trillion parameters, revealing emergent reasoning capabilities and improved sample efficiency through algorithmic and system optimizations like clipped importance sampling and training-inference ratio correction.
key_points: Scaling to 1 trillion parameters significantly enhances sample efficiency and performance ceilings in zero-RL.
The training process involves a sequential discovery phase followed by a sharpening phase.
The model spontaneously develops advanced cognitive behaviors including anthropomorphism, structured formatting, self-verification, parallel reasoning, and context anxiety.
A stable and efficient training pipeline incorporates clipped importance sampling, training-inference ratio correction, and mixed-precision control.
Ring-2.5-1T-Zero achieves competitive performance on seven mathematical benchmarks and produces structured, concise reasoning traces.
summary.why_it_matters: This research provides insights into scaling behaviors of zero-RL models at the trillion-parameter scale, demonstrating emergent reasoning without human-annotated data.

papers.title: KnowAct-GUIClaw: Know Deeply, Act Perfectly, Personal GUI Assistant with Self-Evolving Memory and Skill

summary.tldr: KnowAct-GUIClaw is a novel Know-Route-Act-Reflect framework that enhances OpenClaw with cross-platform GUI interaction and self-evolving memory/skill for improved task automation.
key_points: KnowAct-GUIClaw introduces a Know-Route-Act-Reflect framework to address OpenClaw's limitations in cross-platform GUI interaction and self-evolution.
The framework incorporates a host agent for long-horizon task decomposition and a pluggable GUI subagent with an experience-attributable memory system and self-evolving skill library.
It continuously stores user profiles and feedback to improve the accuracy of task decomposition and tool calls.
KnowAct-GUIClaw achieved 64.1% performance on the MobileWorld benchmark with Kimi-2.6 models, outperforming Seed-2.0-Pro and GPT-5.5.
Knowledgeable memory and execution skills are transferable across base models, improving Kimi-2.6 performance by 8.5%.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework enables more efficient, accurate, and adaptable personal GUI assistants across diverse device ecosystems through continuous learning and cross-platform capabilities.

papers.title: OvisOCR2 Technical Report

summary.tldr: OvisOCR2 is a 0.8B end-to-end document parsing model that generates Markdown from page images, achieving state-of-the-art results on OmniDocBench v1.6 and PureDocBench.
key_points: OvisOCR2 is a 0.8B end-to-end document parsing model that outputs Markdown representations including text, formulas, tables, and visual regions from document page images.
The training regimen includes supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning on a 4B branch with multi-component reward design, on-policy distillation to the 0.8B model, and model fusion.
OvisOCR2 achieved an overall score of 96.58 on OmniDocBench v1.6 and an Avg3 score of 75.06 on PureDocBench, both state-of-the-art.
A data engine combines filtered real-document annotations with synthetic pages derived from HTML sources.
summary.why_it_matters: This model demonstrates the potential of end-to-end document parsing to surpass pipeline methods on complex benchmarks and offers a robust solution for diverse document understanding tasks.

papers.title: AgentCompass: A Unified Evaluation Infrastructure for Agent Capabilities

summary.tldr: AgentCompass is a new open-source, lightweight, and extensible infrastructure for evaluating LLM-based agents, designed to unify fragmented evaluation pipelines and improve reproducibility.
key_points: AgentCompass organizes evaluation into three independent components: Benchmark, Harness, and Environment, allowing flexible configurations without reimplementing execution logic.
It includes a fault-tolerant asynchronous runtime and tools for comprehensive trajectory analysis to diagnose failure modes like reward-hacking.
The infrastructure natively supports over 20 benchmarks across five capability dimensions.
summary.why_it_matters: This infrastructure provides a scalable and reproducible platform for advancing research in LLM-based agent capabilities by addressing current evaluation fragmentation.

papers.title: MetaView: Monocular Novel View Synthesis with Scale-Aware Implicit Geometry Priors

summary.tldr: MetaView is a diffusion-based monocular novel view synthesis framework that combines implicit geometry modeling with minimal explicit 3D cues for large view changes from a single image.
key_points: MetaView uses a diffusion-based framework for monocular novel view synthesis.
It integrates implicit geometry priors from a feed-forward geometry perception network to regularize structure.
Metric depth is leveraged to anchor the generation to a metric scale, ensuring precise controllability.
The method enables rendering under large view changes from a single input image.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach significantly improves geometry consistency and controllability in novel view synthesis, outperforming existing methods in challenging monocular large viewpoint changes.

papers.title: PolicyShiftGuard: Benchmarking and Improving Policy-Adaptive Image Guardrails

summary.tldr: This paper introduces PolicyShiftGuard, a policy-adaptive image guardrail, and PolicyShiftBench, a benchmark for evaluating guardrail adaptation to dynamic safety policies.
key_points: PolicyShiftBench contains 2,000 policy-discriminative instances across 265 images, with each image paired with an average of 7.55 policy-conditioned prompts.
PolicyShiftGuard is a compact policy-conditioned guardrail trained using a two-stage recipe: Randomized Policy SFT (RP-SFT) and Boundary-Pair Policy Adaptation (BP-Adapt).
BP-Adapt utilizes matched prompts for the same image and risk category, employing standard label supervision and a pairwise comparison loss to differentiate blocking from passing policies.
The 7B PolicyShiftGuard model achieves 76.9 Avg. F1 and 72.1 Avg. PSS on PolicyShiftBench, outperforming existing VLMs and specialized guardrails.
PolicyShiftGuard demonstrates improved latency-performance trade-off and transfers effectively to UnSafeBench and SafeEditBench.
summary.why_it_matters: This work enables image guardrails to adapt to evolving safety policies, improving their utility in dynamic real-world deployments.

papers.title: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey

summary.tldr: This survey frames modern self-improving agents as adaptive systems, formalizing self-improvement as a self-induced update operator that modifies model parameters or scaffold components based on experience, aiming for controllable evolution with minimal human input.
key_points: Modern agents are represented as a configuration coupling a foundation model with an operational scaffold (prompts, memory, tools, control logic).
Self-improvement is formalized as a self-induced update operator that commits updates to model parameters or scaffold components.
Prior work is organized by the update target and the signals driving change.
The primary goal of self-improving agents is controllable evolution or adaptation from experience with minimal or no human input.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework provides a structured understanding of how autonomous agents can achieve adaptation and capability gains through experience, moving from research to deployed systems.

papers.title: GigaWorld-Policy-0.5: A Faster and Stronger WAM Empowered by AutoResearch

summary.tldr: GigaWorld-Policy-0.5 enhances World Action Models (WAMs) with an action-centered formulation, mixed AC-WM/WAM training, and a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture for faster, more efficient robot control, achieving 85 ms inference latency.
key_points: GigaWorld-Policy-0.5 uses an action-centered formulation, leveraging future visual dynamics during training but performing action-only decoding at inference to reduce computational overhead.

It adopts a mixed Action-Conditioned World Modeling (AC-WM) and WAM training strategy during pretraining to strengthen visual dynamics-action coupling and improve action representation transferability.
A Mixture-of-Transformers architecture separates visual dynamics modeling and action generation into specialized experts, reducing active computation during action-only inference.
The system achieves 85 ms inference latency on an RTX 4090 setup.
An agent-based AutoResearch pipeline systematically searches training configurations, optimizing experimental setups and reducing hyperparameter tuning time.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables real-time closed-loop deployment of robot policies by significantly improving inference efficiency while preserving the benefits of future visual dynamics for training.

papers.title: Registers Matter for Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers

summary.tldr: Register tokens, known to mitigate high-norm patch-token outliers in ViTs, also benefit Diffusion Transformers (DiTs), particularly in pixel-space, by producing cleaner feature maps at high noise levels.
key_points: DiTs do not exhibit patch-token outliers, unlike ViTs, but still benefit from register tokens.
Register tokens are more effective in pixel-space DiTs than in latent-space DiTs.
Register tokens produce cleaner feature maps at high noise levels in DiTs.
Recent pixel-space DiT architectures implicitly incorporate register-like mechanisms.
Register Guidance is proposed to amplify the contribution of register tokens for improved visual structure and coherence.
summary.why_it_matters: Implementing register tokens or Register Guidance can improve the quality of generated images in pixel-space Diffusion Transformers.

papers.title: Discrete Diffusion Models: A Unified Framework from Tokenization to Generation

summary.tldr: This paper unifies discrete denoising diffusion models (DDMs) by framing them through discrete state space construction, encompassing existing formulations and exposing design trade-offs.
key_points: DDMs offer parallel generation and iterative global refinement for discrete data, contrasting with autoregressive modeling.
The discrete state space construction, including tokenization and vocabulary topology, fundamentally shapes DDMs.
Existing DDM formulations (transition-matrix, masking/absorbing-state, score/ratio-based) are presented as instantiations within this unified framework.
The framework highlights design trade-offs across training objectives, inference algorithms, scaling, systems optimization, and evaluation.
summary.why_it_matters: This unified framework provides a clearer understanding of DDM design choices and their implications, guiding future research and development.

papers.title: Hallo4D: Multi-Modal Hallucination Mitigation for Consistent Spatio-Temporal Generation

summary.tldr: Hallo4D is a model-agnostic framework that mitigates spatio-temporal hallucinations in 3D/4D generation using a generation-detection-correction paradigm leveraging LMMs for consistency optimization.
key_points: Hallo4D employs a generation-detection-correction paradigm, using LMMs to identify and summarize spatial/temporal inconsistencies from multi-view/multi-frame renderings.
A consensus-driven image-space consistency optimization is guided by an LMM-based selector that evaluates candidate corrections via multi-model voting without retraining.
Temporal consistency is enhanced through motion-aware keyframe sampling, LMM-guided initialization, and appearance alignment.
Robustness under challenging viewpoints is improved by incorporating exposure-aware optimization and visibility pruning.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework provides a scalable and generalizable solution for generating consistent 3D and 4D content, addressing issues like duplicated structures, misaligned geometry, jitter, and structural drift.

papers.title: ShortOPD: Recovering Pruned LLMs with Short-to-Long On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: ShortOPD is a novel short-to-long On-Policy Distillation schedule that significantly improves the recovery of pruned LLMs for free-form generation tasks by focusing training on non-repetitive, high-information tokens.
key_points: Structured pruning often causes LLMs to collapse on free-form generation, with greedy pass@1 nearly vanishing, though pass@k recovers substantially.
The primary failure mode in the recoverable regime is suffix repetition, indicating a need for token-level supervision on the compressed model's on-policy states.
ShortOPD mitigates wasted training on repetitive suffixes by detecting teacher-confirmed repetitions and adjusting effective rollout lengths.
ShortOPD achieves 9x the unrecovered score and 1.6-4.4x standard recovery methods, using 25% of training time (8.5 vs. 35.9 hours) and 71% fewer rollout tokens compared to fixed 8192-token rollouts.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables structured pruning to produce deployment-ready LLMs for generation tasks, moving beyond marginal gains on perplexity and multiple-choice benchmarks.

papers.title: Tracing Agentic Failure from the Flow of Success

summary.tldr: OAT is a novel unsupervised failure attribution model for LLM-based agentic systems, using neural controlled differential equations to identify error steps in failure trajectories by learning from successful ones.
key_points: OAT addresses unsupervised failure attribution, training exclusively on successful trajectories to identify error steps at inference time.
The model casts the problem as one-class learning with neural controlled differential equations, modeling successful trajectory dynamics in latent space.
At inference, each step in a failure trajectory receives an anomaly score based on its deviation from learned successful dynamics.
OAT trains on only 100 successful trajectories, achieving 200-5000 times faster performance than prompting-based baselines.
OAT consistently outperforms prompting-based baselines with +20% F1 in-domain and +7% F1 out-of-distribution.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach offers a lightweight, efficient, and scalable method for debugging and improving LLM-based agentic systems without costly step-level failure annotations.

papers.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs

summary.tldr: A new in-place tokenizer expansion method for pre-trained LLMs allows upgrading a model's tokenizer by continuing BPE merges on a multilingual corpus, improving efficiency for underrepresented languages without losing source-checkpoint quality.
key_points: Tokenizer expansion continues existing BPE merges on a multilingual corpus, ensuring new tokens have exact decompositions into source tokens.
Carried-over embedding rows are copied unchanged; new rows are initialized as the mean of their source sub-token embeddings.
A two-stage adaptation (embedding-only training then full-model continued pre-training) recovers source-checkpoint quality.
Applied to LFM2-8B-A1B, the expanded 128K tokenizer reduced token count for Hindi and Vietnamese by approximately 2.4x and 2.6x, respectively (up to 4.0x for Thai).
The method estimates a 2.2-3.7x per-character decode speedup for these languages on reference devices.
summary.why_it_matters: This method significantly improves decode speed and reduces computational overhead for languages underrepresented in initial pre-training, making LLMs more efficient and accessible globally.

papers.title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space

summary.tldr: This paper demonstrates that content danger and physical danger are separable signals in LLM hidden states and introduces PRISM, a probing method for detecting physical risk in embodied agent planning, outperforming LLM judges.
key_points: Content danger (CD) and physical danger (PD) are separable signals in LLM representations across Qwen2.5-3B/7B/14B/32B, Phi-3.5, and SmolLM2, identified via hidden-state direction analysis and random-split null tests.
PRISM, a single-layer L2-regularized logistic probe over full hidden states, achieves 86.2-87.7% accuracy on SafeAgentBench with 11.7-13.7% FPR.
LLM judges over-block safe tasks at 24.7-39.0% FPR on SafeAgentBench, significantly higher than PRISM's FPR.
PhysicalSafetyBench-1K (PSB-1K), a new contrastive benchmark of 1,000 physical-risk pairs without direct harm keywords, was introduced.
On PSB-1K, PRISM achieves 99.6% accuracy and 0.7% FPR, while a Qwen2.5-3B judge rejects 67.8% of safe tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: This research provides a more effective method for ensuring physical safety in LLM-controlled embodied agents, reducing over-blocking of safe tasks compared to current LLM judges.

papers.title: T^2MLR: Transformer with Temporal Middle-Layer Recurrence

summary.tldr: T2MLR introduces temporal middle-layer recurrence into Transformers, allowing intermediate reasoning states to persist across decoding steps with minimal inference overhead, outperforming baseline Transformers in pretraining and multi-hop reasoning.
key_points: T2MLR fuses a cached middle layer representation from the previous token directly into an earlier layer of the current token position.
Applying recurrence to a localized middle-layer block (as little as 20% of the network) often outperforms full-layer recurrence.
T2MLR does not require pretraining from scratch; retrofitting into an existing pretrained 1.7B Transformer and finetuning improves math reasoning.
T2MLR consistently outperforms data- and parameter-matched Transformer baselines across natural-language pretraining and multi-hop reasoning finetuning.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach offers a practical method to enhance latent reasoning in Transformers by improving the persistence of intermediate computation with low overhead and without extensive retraining.

papers.title: Long-Context Fine-Tuning with Limited VRAM

summary.tldr: Hierarchical Global Attention (HGA) combined with segment-wise backpropagation and tiered KV storage enables fine-tuning of large language models with long contexts on limited VRAM.
key_points: HGA with segment-wise backpropagation and tiered KV storage allows training sequences up to 16,384 tokens on a 16 GB GPU, while dense attention fails at 4,096 tokens.
Only the active segment remains differentiable in VRAM; older KV is detached to RAM or NVMe, and HGA loads a bounded set of exact historical tokens for each query block.
On Qwen3-8B with 4-bit QLoRA, HGA achieves 16,384 tokens with 15.28 GB peak VRAM during training and 131,072 tokens during evaluation on a 16 GB Quadro RTX 5000.
HGA-trained adapters achieve comparable perplexity (2.7405 nat) to dense-trained adapters (2.7383 nat) at 2K training length, outperforming the stock model (2.9541 nat).
HGA training is marginally faster at 2K tokens/s (217.75 vs. 207.02 tokens/s for dense) and throughput ratio improves with context length due to constant attended historical set per token.
summary.why_it_matters: This method significantly extends the context length for fine-tuning large language models on commodity hardware, reducing VRAM requirements and improving training efficiency for long sequences.

papers.title: OmniaBench: Benchmarking General AI Agents Across Diverse Scenarios

summary.tldr: OmniaBench is a new benchmark for general AI agents, featuring diverse scenarios, explicit state spaces, and a hierarchical taxonomy derived from real-world applications, designed to evaluate capabilities across various domains and identify limitations.
key_points: OmniaBench constructs a hierarchical taxonomy from app stores, product documents, industry resources, and Web retrieval, spanning ToC, ToB, and ToE with 90 level-1 and 354 level-2 domains.
The benchmark includes 1,431 tasks, with a challenging subset of 644 tasks, synthesized through four routes: DAG, DAG-S, Solver, and Program, within executable environments.
A ten-dimensional capability taxonomy and eight compositional atomic difficulty factors are introduced for fine-grained evaluation and analysis.
Current frontier models, Claude-Sonnet-5 and GPT-5.6-Sol, achieved Overall Pass@1 scores of 58.54 and 57.14, respectively, indicating substantial challenges.
Analysis reveals persistent limitations in planning, constraint maintenance, and adaptive correction across domains and capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark provides a comprehensive and diagnostic tool for characterizing the current capability boundaries of general AI agents, guiding future development.

papers.title: VarRate: Training-Free Variable-Rate KV Cache Compression for Long-Context LLMs

summary.tldr: VarRate is a training-free KV cache compression method for long-context LLMs that assigns variable low-rank budgets to tokens based on query salience, keeping all tokens at a non-zero rank.
key_points: VarRate avoids token eviction, which causes 11-15 point accuracy collapse in token-selection methods under query-agnostic reuse.
VarRate degrades by only 3.5-5.5 points where query-aware selection collapses, by keeping every token at a non-zero rank.
At 20% budget on LongBench, VarRate stays within 0.8 points of uncompressed Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B.
VarRate significantly outperforms its uniform-rank ablation on both Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B.
VarRate is accuracy-equivalent to KVzip in three of four settings and within a point overall, with approximately one-eighth the prefill overhead.
summary.why_it_matters: VarRate offers a more robust and accurate training-free KV cache compression solution for long-context LLMs by preventing token loss and efficiently allocating memory.

papers.title: Relevant and Irrelevant: A Renormalization Group Analysis of Transformer Attention

summary.tldr: This paper applies Wilsonian renormalization group theory to Transformer attention, classifying it as a relevant or irrelevant operator based on data correlation length and deriving testable predictions for fixed-point geometry and perturbation decay.
key_points: Attention is strongly relevant for long correlation chains, closing a residual loss gap and driving a phase transition in representation space with effective rank jumping above input dimensionality at layer 1.
Attention is irrelevant for short correlation chains, leading to the same loss and fixed-point geometry as the MLP, but contracting perturbations faster.
The first-layer head (L0H0) dominates the transition, accounting for over 4 times the representational shift of subsequent heads.

In long correlation regimes, the Transformer selectively preserves slow Markov modes (5.4x dynamic range in decay length vs. 1.3x for MLP); in short correlation regimes, it suppresses all modes faster than the MLP without spectral selectivity.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding attention's relevance based on data spectral structure allows for more informed Transformer design and application, optimizing performance for specific data types.

papers.title: D-cut: Adaptive Verification Depth Pruning for Batched Speculative Decoding

summary.tldr: D-Cut is an adaptive pruning method for batched speculative decoding that optimizes verification depth across concurrent requests to improve LLM inference speedup, especially under high concurrency.
key_points: D-Cut addresses the issue of long drafts wasting computation on rejected tokens in batched speculative decoding, which can make it slower than autoregressive decoding under high concurrency.
It performs cross-request pruning, adaptively allocating the verification budget based on draft confidence across concurrent requests.
D-Cut incorporates a runtime cost model to adapt its pruning depth to the target deployment environment, considering factors like GPU architecture and parallelism strategy.
Experiments show D-Cut improves average speedup from 1.26x to 1.65x under high concurrency and achieves up to 3.0x speedup over autoregressive decoding on MoE models.
summary.why_it_matters: D-Cut significantly enhances the efficiency of LLM inference in high-concurrency environments by reducing wasted computation and adapting to deployment specifics.

papers.title: Beyond Entropy: Correctness-Aware Advantage Shaping via Contrastive Policy Optimization

summary.tldr: Contrastive Policy Optimization (CPO) uses token-level contrastive disagreement between reference-guided and vanilla generation distributions for correctness-aware advantage shaping in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), outperforming entropy-based methods.
key_points: CPO employs token-level contrastive disagreement between a reference-guided generation distribution and a vanilla generation distribution to shape advantage.
This contrastive disagreement serves as a reliable indicator of token-level correctness, distinguishing useful uncertainty from detrimental confusion.
On-policy Distillation is a special case of CPO where an external teacher model instantiates the posterior distribution.
CPO resolves the zero-advantage problem, a limitation of some RL methods.
Experiments show CPO substantially outperforms entropy-based RLVR methods on in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves the effectiveness of reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by providing a more accurate signal for correctness, leading to better performance and generalization.

papers.title: Answer-Conditioned Chains of Thought Degrade Verifiable-Reasoning Distillation in Large Language Models

summary.tldr: Answer-conditioned chain-of-thought generation degrades verifiable-reasoning distillation in LLMs, leading to lower accuracy, especially on difficult problems, due to backward rationalization.
key_points: Training a strong instruction-tuned reasoning model on its own answer-conditioned chains sharply lowers its verifiable-reasoning accuracy.
The accuracy loss grows with problem difficulty, reaching approximately 27 points on the hardest competition problems.
Answer-conditioned chains exhibit backward rationalization, deriving from the shown answer rather than independently, with early final-answer statements as a measurable symptom.
The degradation is a property of the data, not the generator, and transfers across teacher families, affecting eight thinking models from four families.
The 'rationalize-toward' instruction, not just answer visibility, causes the degradation.
summary.why_it_matters: To maintain reasoning accuracy in LLM distillation, chains of thought should be generated answer-blind, as correctness filters cannot detect this data damage.

security.title: Least privilege for AI agents: Identity, access, and tool binding

summary.tldr: AI agents require lifecycle-managed identities, explicit roles, tightly scoped permissions, and preconfigured tool usage to mitigate risks like unauthorized data access and privilege escalation.
key_points: Agents operating without managed identities and least-privilege RBAC can access or modify sensitive data beyond intended permissions.
Scope creep in agent permissions, where initial read-only roles expand to include write access, is a common problem leading to overly broad assignments.
Agents with access to multiple tools can correlate data across systems and take unauthorized actions, resulting in broader effective permissions than individually evaluated.
Ambiguity in whether an agent acts under its own identity, a delegated user scope, or a mix, complicates accountability and auditability during incidents.
Best practices include treating agents as first-class principals with lifecycle-managed identities, explicit roles, tight scope, and safe tool binding via a manifest.
summary.why_it_matters: Failure to properly manage AI agent identities and permissions can lead to significant security risks, including unauthorized data access, unintended modifications, privilege escalation, and compromised auditability.

Agentic AI involves extensive network transfers per request.
Infrastructure must rapidly move, protect, retrieve, and reuse data to support concurrent agents and persistent context.
summary.why_it_matters: The complex, multi-step nature of agentic AI requires significant infrastructure changes to manage data flow and processing efficiently.
